newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends mostly lower on weather, plantings.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends mostly lower on weather, plantings.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended mostly lower on Monday with new crop down amid perceptions weather patterns were conducive to crop development and plantings were progressing rapidly, pit sources said.
The May contract ended higher on short covering ahead of expiration Tuesday and on firm cash basis levels. USDA's weekly export inspections data was also deemed supportive.

Traders noted forecasts called for mostly dry, cool weather from Tuesday to Friday in much of the U.S. Midwest. That scenario, combined with expected weekend showers, should be beneficial to corn development, they said.
New crop was also pressured by ideas Monday's USDA weekly crop progress report would show between 80 and 85 percent of the corn crop was planted as of Sunday.
But losses were limited by ideas it was too early in the growing season to bank on ideal growing conditions.
"It's too early to be bearish on this weather," one trader said. "Maybe if it were June 19 but it's May 19. We can't take out too much of the weather premium."
Corn ended five cents per bushel higher to 1-1/2 cents lower with July unchanged at $2.84-1/2 a bushel and new crop December down 3/4 at $2.65-1/2.

Friday's USDA seven state cattle-on-feed report was somewhat bearish for corn futures. The report pegged April placements at 12 percent above a year ago, below the average of analysts' estimates for a 13.9 percent placements increase.

Export news was mildly supportive with USDA's weekly export inspections figure at 28,274,000 bushels, above trade expectations for 22 million to 27 million. Traders also noted Thailand was scrambling to buy corn in transit after the government approved 200,000 tonnes of tariff-free imports.
"The exports were above what the trade was looking for," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities in Iowa.

On the day, funds were sellers early but commercial buying underpinned nearbys. Traders said FIMAT Futures sold four milion bushels December and 1.5 million July, Refco Inc sold three million July and Lee B. Stern sold one million July.
Cargill Inc bought one million each July and December.
Cargill and Continental Grain each spread one million July/May at six cents, premium May.

In options trade, FIMAT bought 500 July $2.70 puts and sold 500 July $2.60 puts at one to 2-3/4 cents. E.D. and F. Man International sold 400 July $2.90 calls and 400 July $2.80 puts at 10-1/2 to 11 cents.
Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 48,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 51,510.
